title: Closed slice comparison with transported pro-etale coefficients
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $u:U\to X$ be an object of its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use its canonical site equivalence $U_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] and the natural inverse-image identification $\delta_G:u^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_U$ for sheaves of sets, abelian groups and rings [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction]. Let $\mathcal O$ and $\mathcal B$ be arbitrary sheaves of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, respectively, and let $c:u^{-1}\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B$ be a ring isomorphism. Set $b=c\circ\delta_{\mathcal O}^{-1}:\mathcal O|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B$. Let $r:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O|_U)$ be exact derived slice restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction, def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and let $E_b:D(\mathcal O|_U)\to D(\mathcal B)$ be the termwise scalar-transport equivalence, which leaves underlying abelian sheaves unchanged and replaces an action by $s\cdot m=b^{-1}(s)m$. Put $F=Lu^*:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal B)$ for the exact module inverse image defined using $c$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. All these are ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

The maps $\delta_G$, with these actions, induce a natural isomorphism $F\xrightarrow{\sim}E_b\circ r$. This isomorphism identifies the canonical strong symmetric monoidal tensor and unit comparisons of $F$ with those of slice restriction followed by scalar transport. Use the ordinary derived tensor, internal Hom $H$ and tensor--Hom transposition $\operatorname{tr}$ of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], and write $H_{\mathcal B},\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal B}$ for the corresponding structures over $\mathcal B$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$h_{L,M}:F H(L,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{\mathcal B}(FL,FM),$$
which under $F\cong E_b r$ is the scalar transport of the canonical slice internal-Hom comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Write $\rho_{L,M}:F(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}M)\xrightarrow{\sim}FL\otimes^{\mathbf L}FM$ for the canonical tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and $\sigma$ for the Koszul symmetry. For all $A,L,M\in D(\mathcal O)$ and $g:A\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M$, the following identities hold:
$$F(\operatorname{ev}_{L,M})\circ\rho_{H(L,M),L}^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_{FL,FM}\circ(h_{L,M}\otimes1),$$
$$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal B}(F(g)\circ\rho_{A,L}^{-1})=h_{L,M}\circ F(\operatorname{tr}(g)),$$
$$\rho_{M,L}\circ F(\sigma_{L,M})=\sigma_{FL,FM}\circ\rho_{L,M}.$$
No constancy of $\mathcal O$, boundedness of complexes, quasi-compactness or bound on irreducible components is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the normalized ordinary comparison by the map/pullback module adjunction and uniqueness of the left adjoint. Use the separate monoidal descent theorem with that ordinary comparison to obtain chain, K-flat, tensor, unit and symmetry data.

Scalar restriction along b inverse is an equivalence, hence so is its exact derived functor. For any strong tensor equivalence F, the closed mate is invertible: on Hom out of F(A) its postcomposition is the composite of the source closed bijection, full faithfulness, tensor comparison and target closed bijection. Essential surjectivity and Yoneda yield invertibility. Apply to scalar transport. The normalized restriction mate is invertible by the separate slice-closed-mates lemma. Naturality packages both into natural isomorphisms.

Cancel the invertible comparison on tensor factors in the normalized tensor square to put it in the direction of scalarBaseChangeHom_tower. The generic closed-mate composition formula (proved here by transposition and naturality, reusing the private argument of ScalarHomComparisonTower), applied to restriction, scalar transport and the ordinary comparison, gives hom_transport. Every factor is an isomorphism, so the pullback mate is invertible. Package it as the required natural Hom isomorphism.

The closed adjunction says that uncurrying the transpose of any arrow returns that arrow. Applied to transported evaluation this proves the evaluation equation. Naturality of the tensor comparison and the source uncurry identity prove the transpose equation. Combine them with the monoidal descent symmetry equation and all retained normalizations.

theorem proEtaleCoefficientSliceClosedComparison {X : Scheme.{u}} (U : X.ProEt)
    (O : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (B : Sheaf (ProEt.topology U.left) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (c : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage U.hom CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj O ≅ B)
    (delta : ProEtaleObjectRestrictionComparison U CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (S : CoefficientClosedStructure (proEtaleCoefficientHom X O))
    (SR : CoefficientClosedStructure (proEtaleCoefficientHom U.left (proEtaleSliceRing U O)))
    (SB : CoefficientClosedStructure (proEtaleCoefficientHom U.left B))
    (T : CoefficientTensorModels.{u + 1, u + 1, u} (ProEt.topology X) O S)
    (TR : CoefficientTensorModels.{u + 1, u + 1, u} (ProEt.topology U.left)
      (proEtaleSliceRing U O) SR)
    (TB : CoefficientTensorModels.{u + 1, u + 1, u} (ProEt.topology U.left) B SB)
    (beta : @SymmetricCategory (DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules X O)) _ S.monoidal)
    (betaB : @SymmetricCategory (DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules U.left B)) _ SB.monoidal)
    (_coherence : RingedDerivedTensorCoherence.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (ProEt.topology X) O S T beta)
    (_coherenceB : RingedDerivedTensorCoherence.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (ProEt.topology U.left) B SB TB betaB) :
    ∃ d : ProEtaleCoefficientSliceComparison.Data U O B c delta S SR SB T TR TB,
      ProEtaleCoefficientSliceComparison.Normalized U O B c delta S SR SB T TR TB d ∧
      CoefficientClosedComparisonLaws S SB (proEtaleRingDerivedPullback U.hom O B c)
        (ProEtaleCoefficientSliceComparison.rho U O B c S SB T TB)
        d.homComparison beta betaB
